metadata.scenario: A client calls arguing about a higher than expected fee on their account statement. Category: Billing. Flags: billing_dispute.

transcription.text: Thank you for calling CareFirst Home Health, this is Margaret. How can I help you today? Hi Margaret, this is Michael Brown. I'm calling about a billing issue I noticed on my father's account. Hi Michael, I’m glad you reached out. Can you tell me more about the issue? Yes, I received a statement and the fee is higher than what I expected. I'm sorry to hear that. Let me look up your father's account. Can I have his name and date of birth, please? Sure, his name is John Brown, and he was born on January 15, 1948. Thank you, Michael. One moment while I pull up that information. [pauses] Okay, I see the account here. Great. So, what’s going on with the charges? It looks like there was an increase in the fees for wound care and medication management services. But I was quoted a lower price when we started the services! I understand your concern. Let’s go over the details to clarify the differences. Yes, please. I want to understand why it's higher now. The increase is due to an adjustment in our pricing structure, which was communicated in a previous statement. I must have missed that. Can you resend me all the updated billing information? Absolutely, I can send that to your email or a physical address, whichever you prefer. Email is best. It's michael.brown@email.com. Got it, I’ll send that information over right after our call. Thank you. Is there anything else I can do to lower these charges? We can review the services being provided and see if there are any adjustments we can make for your father’s care. I’d appreciate that. He needs wound care and medication management, but I want to keep costs manageable. Certainly, we can have a care coordinator discuss your options. Would you like me to set up a follow-up call? Yes, that would be helpful. Great! I can have Lisa Chen, our Care Coordinator, call you on Monday. Does that work for you? Yes, Monday works. Thank you for your help today, Margaret. You're welcome, Michael. We’re here to support you and your father. I appreciate that. Talk to you on Monday! Talk to you then! Have a great day. You too, bye! Goodbye!
